operation_title: This method updates partially the profile of a given NF instance.

request_body.description: It contains the list of changes to be made to the profile of the NF Instance, according to the JSON PATCH format specified in IETF RFC 6902 [13].

response_body.description: Upon success, a response body is returned containing the updated profile of the NF Instance.
Successful response sent when there is no need to provide a full updated profile of the NF Instance (e.g., in the Heart-Beat operation response described in subclause 5.2.2.3.2).

notes: This method shall support the URI query parameters specified in table 6.1.3.3.3.3-1.
No query parameters are defined for this method.
This method shall support the request data structures specified in table 6.1.3.3.3.2 and the response data structures and response codes specified in table 6.1.3.3.3.3-3.

NOTE: The mandatory HTTP error status codes for the PATCH method listed in Table 5.2.7.1-1 of 3GPP TS 29.500 [4] other than those specified in the table above also apply, with a ProblemDetails data type (see subclause 5.2.7 of 3GPP TS 29.500 [4]).

constraints.statement: The request body shall contain exactly one PatchDocument.
The PATCH operation shall not define any query parameters.
A successful response shall use either 200 OK or 204 No Content.
A 200 OK response shall include an NFProfile response body.
A 204 No Content response shall not include a response body.
The request URI shall include the nfInstanceID path variable.
The nfInstanceID path variable identifies a specific NF instance.
The PatchDocument shall use the JSON Patch format defined in RFC 6902.
On error responses, the operation shall support the mandatory HTTP error status codes applicable to PATCH in 3GPP TS 29.500, with ProblemDetails as the error body type.
